old_caption: The video depicts a close-up view of a person's hands assembling a molecular model on a white surface. The model consists of metallic spheres connected by rods, forming a hexagonal lattice structure. The person's hands are seen attaching a rod to a sphere, extending the structure. In the background, there is a box filled with additional metallic spheres, suggesting that these are components used to build or modify the molecular model. The setting appears to be a workspace or laboratory environment, indicated by the clean and organized surface. The focus remains on the hands and the molecular model throughout the video, highlighting the interaction between the person and the object. There are no significant changes in the scenery or the introduction of new elements; the video maintains a consistent perspective on the hands and the molecular model.

caption: The video depicts a top-down view of a white tabletop where two hands assemble a flat hexagonal lattice of shiny metallic spheres linked by short rods. An open box of spare spheres rests in the upper-left corner. The left hand pinches a free sphere at the lower edge of the sheet while the right hand holds a loose rod beside it. The right hand brings that rod into contact with the sphere so a new rod extends toward the lower-right, the left hand steadying the sphere while the right hand aligns the far end. After this rod is seated, the structure below the sheet suddenly appears as a closed six-membered ring. The added spheres and rods are not shown in continuous motion but appear without intermediate placement frames. The left hand releases the sphere and drifts toward the left edge of the lattice, while the right hand holds the right-vertex sphere of the new ring to steady it.
